key_insight: A two-phase causal discovery analysis found that steel resistance spot-weld signal morphology is driven mainly by alloying content, sheet thickness, and electrode geometry rather than by all stack-up details.
engineering_relevance: These causal dependencies can help engineers interpret high-frequency weld signals and tune process settings for more robust quality control across diverse materials and configurations.
method: Analyzed 15,096 representative time-series profiles from more than 1.8 million welds
Applied a two-phase causal discovery framework to infer structural signal drivers
Used time-series clustering to handle high-dimensional, multicollinear stack-up data
evidence_signal: The study reports that increased alloying content shifts resistance peaks earlier and suppresses secondary peaks, thickness scales resistance/displacement/force amplitudes, and reducing tip face diameter from 8 to 6 mm raises the initial resistance peak by 9%.
watch_item: The findings are derived from representative profiles and may still require validation before being generalized to new machines, materials, or production environments.
paper_title: Causal discovery of signal morphology drivers in steel resistance spot welding: a high-dimensional data analysis
